record.title: China’s NDRC and five ministries announce 136 major application-scenario projects
record.summary: China’s National Development and Reform Commission and five other central departments announced a first portfolio of 136 major application-scenario projects on 20 October 2026. The NDRC says the portfolio spans five categories and involves more than 1,700 technologies, 1,200 products and 2,200 standards or specifications; it also describes plans to open eligible validation opportunities to private and smaller firms and to support follow-through. A Beijing government article names five municipal projects in the list, including a 6G validation environment and an industrial-network/data-security agent service. These sources establish the announcement and selected examples, not the complete project list, AI-specific share, project funding, operational status, user access or measured technical and economic outcomes.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: On 20 October 2026, China's National Development and Reform Commission and five other central departments announced a first list of 136 major application-scenario projects. The NDRC release says the portfolio spans five categories and involves more than 1,700 technologies, 1,200 products and 2,200 standards or specifications.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The NDRC says it intends to open eligible validation opportunities to private and small and medium-sized enterprises and to follow with coordination, factor support, reforms and regulatory-capacity measures. The sources describe planned implementation, not completed access or support.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: A Beijing municipal government article identifies five Beijing-led projects in the national list, including a 6G validation environment and an industrial-network and data-security agent public-service scenario. The article describes the projects; it does not report measured AI performance or economic outcomes.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected sources do not establish the complete project-level list, the AI-specific share of the portfolio, project-level appropriations, operating status, actual user access, baselines or measured technical, productivity, safety or economic outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The complete national project-level list and each project's responsible organization and scope were not available in the inspected official pages.
The announcement and explainer describe intended support and access but provide no project-level appropriations, procurement awards, executed contracts or disbursements.
No user counts, operating status, baseline, evaluation protocol or measured technical, safety, productivity or economic outcome was inspected.

brief.importance_rationale: If the portfolio is implemented as described, a central-government program spanning 136 cross-sector test and demonstration projects could influence AI adoption and commercialization across major industries and public services. The score reflects the potential consequence of the announced program; the sources do not establish its AI-specific share, funding, operation or outcomes.
limitations: The NDRC announcement is direct evidence of the policy announcement and its stated aggregate scope, not of project completion or impact.
The NDRC/State Information Center explainer describes future funding and access measures; no appropriation, award or disbursement record was inspected.
The Beijing municipal article provides local examples but not a complete national list or an AI-specific breakdown.
The inspected sources report no evaluation methods, baselines or measured technical, safety, productivity or economic outcomes.

brief.summary: China’s National Development and Reform Commission and five other central departments announced a first portfolio of 136 major application-scenario projects on 20 October 2026. The NDRC says the portfolio spans five categories and involves more than 1,700 technologies, 1,200 products and 2,200 standards or specifications; it also describes plans to open eligible validation opportunities to private and smaller firms and to support follow-through. A Beijing government article names five municipal projects in the list, including a 6G validation environment and an industrial-network/data-security agent service. These sources establish the announcement and selected examples, not the complete project list, AI-specific share, project funding, operational status, user access or measured technical and economic outcomes.

technical.claimed_result: The NDRC describes the portfolio as a way to accelerate validation, application and adoption; these are policy objectives, not measured results.
technical.demonstrated_result: The original-language NDRC release confirms the announcement, listed portfolio size, five category coverage and aggregate technology/product/standard counts. The other inspected sources provide examples and describe planned funding and access measures.
technical.implementation_status: Announced by six central departments on 20 October 2026. NDRC and its explainer describe follow-up support and SME access as planned measures; implementation and project delivery remain unverified.
technical.mechanism: The program groups major use-case and validation projects across new sectors, industrial upgrading, sector applications, social governance and public-service/livelihood domains. It is intended to create real-world validation opportunities and support scaling, with some opportunities potentially opened to private and smaller firms.
technical.regime: A first national portfolio of 136 projects across five broad categories in China. The inspected sources do not identify the complete project-level scope or the AI-specific share.
technical.reproducibility: The announcement, portfolio counts and stated plans are inspectable in official Chinese-language pages. Operational claims would require project-level primary records and evaluation data.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched baseline or pre-program comparison is reported in the inspected sources; no adoption or impact comparison is asserted.

brief.title: China’s NDRC and five ministries announce 136 major application-scenario projects
brief.why_it_matters: The portfolio shows a central-government effort to organize real-world validation and demonstration projects across industry and public services. If implementation gives firms access to operating environments and resources, it could influence how emerging technologies move from development into deployment. The current sources report a broad project portfolio but do not establish what share is AI-specific, what has been funded or operated, or whether any project has produced measurable outcomes.
